USER: Build me a photo-realistic, highly interactive 3D digital twin of Earth.
ASSISTANT (message): I'll build this as a self-contained WebGL app — a Three.js globe with real NASA-derived 8K satellite imagery, day/night terminator computed from the actual sun position, animated clouds, atmospheric scattering, live ISS tracking, and location search. Let me start by checking the workspace and pulling down the assets.
ASSISTANT (tool call) PowerShell input={"command": "Get-ChildItem -Force D:\\physics\\earth | Select-Object Name, Length", "description": "List files in working directory"}
TOOL RESULT: (PowerShell completed with no output)

content.thinking:
The user wants a photo‑realistic, highly interactive 3D digital twin of Earth. I’ve already described the architecture: a self‑contained WebGL app using Three.js, with NASA‑derived 8K satellite imagery, day/night terminator, animated clouds, atmospheric scattering, live ISS tracking, and a location search. The next logical step is to gather the required assets—high‑resolution textures for the globe, clouds, night side, stars, and also normal and specular maps for realistic lighting.

I tried to list the current contents of the working directory with a PowerShell `Get-ChildItem` call on `D:\physics\earth`. The tool returned no output, which means the directory either does not exist yet or is empty. Since I need a place to store the textures and supporting files, I must create the appropriate folder structure first. The project layout I have in mind includes separate subfolders for textures, JavaScript source, CSS, and any library dependencies. Therefore, I should make directories:
- `/d/physics/earth/textures`
- `/d/physics/earth/lib`
- `/d/physics/earth/js`
- `/d/physics/earth/css`

The path uses the Unix‑style `/d/` mount that the environment maps to the Windows `D:` drive, so `mkdir -p` will work for nested creation.

Once the directories exist, I need to download the texture files. I have identified reliable sources:
- The 8K day map from Solar System Scope (`https://www.solarsystemscope.com/textures/download/8k_earth_daymap.jpg`).
- The 8K night map from the same site.
- The 8K cloud map.
- A star field image (`8k_stars_milky_way.jpg`) for the background.
- Normal and specular maps from the official Three.js examples (`earth_normal_2048.jpg` and `earth_specular_2048.jpg`).

I will use `curl -sL --fail -o <filename> <url>` for each, ensuring silent operation, following redirects, and failing on HTTP errors. All downloads should go into the `textures` directory I just created. After issuing all curl commands, I’ll echo a marker (`TEXTURES_DONE`) so I can verify that the background process completed, and then list the directory contents with `ls -la` to confirm the files are present.

Because the downloads are relatively large (8K images are several megabytes each), I’ll run the whole command in the background (`run_in_background: true`). This lets me continue with other setup steps (e.g., scaffolding HTML/JS files) while the assets download.

Thus, the appropriate next action is a Bash command that creates the folder hierarchy, changes into the textures folder, performs all the curl downloads, echoes a completion token, and lists the files. This aligns perfectly with the plan to prepare the assets before coding the Three.js scene.

arguments.command: mkdir -p /d/physics/earth/textures /d/physics/earth/lib /d/physics/earth/js /d/physics/earth/css && cd /d/physics/earth/textures && curl -sL --fail -o 8k_earth_daymap.jpg https://www.solarsystemscope.com/textures/download/8k_earth_daymap.jpg && curl -sL --fail -o 8k_earth_nightmap.jpg https://www.solarsystemscope.com/textures/download/8k_earth_nightmap.jpg && curl -sL --fail -o 8k_earth_clouds.jpg https://www.solarsystemscope.com/textures/download/8k_earth_clouds.jpg && curl -sL --fail -o 8k_stars_milky_way.jpg https://www.solarsystemscope.com/textures/download/8k_stars_milky_way.jpg && curl -sL --fail -o earth_normal_2048.jpg https://threejs.org/examples/textures/planets/earth_normal_2048.jpg && curl -sL --fail -o earth_specular_2048.jpg https://threejs.org/examples/textures/planets/earth_specular_2048.jpg && echo TEXTURES_DONE && ls -la
